findings.documented: append the API key as a query parameter: ?api_key=IVY26-...
findings.actual: a key in the query string is rejected with 401 "send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter"; the key must be sent in the X-API-Key header
findings.how_found: called GET /v1/listings?api_key=... before writing any code and read the 401 detail
findings.impact: every request written from the docs fails with 401

findings.documented: response is {token, token_type, expires_in: 86400, user: {email, name}}; tokens last 24 hours and there is no refresh flow
findings.actual: response is {access_token, refresh_token, token_type, expires_in: 900, refresh_url: "/auth/refresh", user: {email}}; the access token expires after 15 minutes and user has no name
findings.how_found: logged in with curl and decoded the token payload (exp - iat = 900 s); watched a request fail after expiry
findings.impact: an app that reads body.token gets undefined, and an app that logs in once stops working 15 minutes later

findings.documented: not documented; the reference says there is no refresh flow
findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh with body {"refresh_token": "..."} returns a new access_token and refresh_token; the refresh token lasts 7 days. Sending the refresh token as a Bearer header gives 422, and using it as an access token gives 401 "refresh tokens are not accepted here"
findings.how_found: the login response advertises refresh_url; tried body and header variants
findings.impact: needed to keep a session alive past 15 minutes

findings.documented: invalidates the current token server side
findings.actual: returns {"ok": true, "note": "tokens are stateless; discard them client side"}; the same access token keeps working afterwards, and the refresh token still refreshes
findings.how_found: called /v1/me with the token before and after POST /auth/logout
findings.impact: logging out does not revoke a leaked token; clients must delete tokens themselves

findings.documented: collection endpoints take page (1-indexed) and limit, and respond with {total, page, page_size, results}
findings.actual: page is silently ignored (page=2 returns offset 0 again); paging is by offset and limit, and responses are {limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results}
findings.how_found: requested page=2 and compared first ids with page=1, then tried offset
findings.impact: following the docs returns the first page forever; nothing past record 20 can be reached

findings.documented: limit maximum is 200
findings.actual: limit is capped at 50: limit=200 and limit=500 both return 50 records with "limit": 50 in the body
findings.how_found: requested limit=200 and read the echoed limit and count
findings.impact: clients that assume 200 per page skip three quarters of every page

findings.documented: total is the exact number of records matching your filters; fetch total/limit pages to get everything
findings.actual: total under-reports by about 6% on every collection: /v1/listings says 3577 but serves 3800 records, /v1/rentals says 1365 but serves 1450, /v1/projects says 414 but serves 440 (filtered totals are short the same way). Only has_more tells you when the last page is reached
findings.how_found: paged every endpoint with offset until has_more was false and counted distinct ids
findings.impact: stopping at total drops 223 listings, 85 rentals and 26 projects

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns a single listing
findings.actual: 404 Not Found; the single listing lives at GET /v1/listings/{id}
findings.how_found: called the documented path, then the plural form
findings.impact: detail pages built from the docs 404

findings.documented: returns up to ten comparable listings
findings.actual: 404 Not Found for every listing id, at /v1/listings/{id}/similar and /v1/listing/{id}/similar
findings.how_found: called both path forms with a known listing id
findings.impact: no "similar listings" strip is possible from the API

findings.documented: GET/POST /v1/favourites with body {"id": ...} and DELETE /v1/favourites/{id}
findings.actual: 404 Not Found (also /v1/favorites). Saved listings live at GET/POST /v1/saved and DELETE /v1/saved/{id}; POST needs {"listing_id": ...} and {"id": ...} is rejected with 422
findings.how_found: called the documented path, tried common alternatives, read the 422 body
findings.impact: saving listings cannot work from the docs

findings.documented: returns pre-computed city aggregates (total_listings, median_price, median_price_per_sqft, by_locality, by_bhk)
findings.actual: 404 Not Found; no analytics path exists under /v1. The aggregates have to be computed from the full listing set
findings.how_found: called the documented path and nearby variants
findings.impact: an insights screen has to compute its own numbers

findings.documented: not documented
findings.actual: GET /v1/me returns the user, city_id, city, assigned_locality and reference_date for the key
findings.how_found: probed after seeing the key is city-scoped
findings.impact: useful for showing the city in the app

findings.documented: not documented
findings.actual: GET /v1/localities returns the city and each locality with a listing_count
findings.how_found: probed for a way to populate a locality filter
findings.impact: none; convenience endpoint

findings.documented: returns active sale listings only; inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side, so anything returned is safe to show
findings.actual: returns every record with an is_live flag; 802 of 3800 records have is_live false
findings.how_found: counted is_live across the full crawl
findings.impact: showing the feed as-is advertises 802 listings that are no longer available

findings.documented: each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property
findings.actual: 3800 records describe 3230 properties. 570 records re-post an existing flat, usually on another portal, with the building name varied ("The X", "X Apartments", "X Phase 1", case, hyphens), coordinates jittered by up to ~100 m, carpet area within 2% and price within a few percent; every other layout field is identical. Pairs shown in evidence
findings.how_found: clustered records with identical layout (locality, type, bedrooms, bathrooms, balconies, floor, total floors, facing, furnishing, parking) and near coordinates; the cluster count was the same for every distance threshold from 150 m to 1 km
findings.impact: listing counts and market statistics are inflated by 18%

findings.documented: posted_by_contact is the seller's verified contact number; is_verified means the operations team has checked the listing
findings.actual: 205 listings are lead-generation fakes. They come from 7 phone numbers, each posting under 3-5 different agent or agency names across all portals and localities. Every one of them is marked is_verified and is_live, and they are priced at 27-83% of the market rate for their locality and type. 25 of them copy a genuine listing at roughly half its price. Genuine agencies also share numbers, but at market prices
findings.how_found: grouped listings by phone number, then compared price per sq ft with the locality median for each group
findings.impact: buyers are sent to fraudulent contacts, and the verified badge vouches for them

findings.documented: listing fields describe real properties: price in rupees, floor within total_floors, carpet area within super built-up area, posted_at in the past
findings.actual: 49 records are impossible: 7 with negative prices, 7 with a price under Rs 20,000 for a whole property, 7 on a floor above the building's top floor, 7 with carpet area larger than super built-up area, 7 apartments/builder floors with zero bedrooms and zero bathrooms, 7 posted after the reference date (up to May 2027), 7 with latitude and longitude swapped
findings.how_found: checked each field against physical constraints and against the other fields of the same record
findings.impact: these records break price sorting, price filters and every average

findings.documented: area is in square feet, integer, everywhere in the API
findings.actual: magichomes listings posted from 2026-06-01 give carpet_area and super_built_up_area in square metres (41-189 for 1-5 BHK instead of 440-2000). All 306 such records are affected and none posted earlier. The server itself sorts sort_by=carpet_area as if they were converted (216 is ordered between 2392 and 2298)
findings.how_found: plotted carpet area by website and bedroom count; magichomes alone had a second cluster ten times smaller, split exactly by posting date
findings.impact: those flats look ten times smaller and ten times pricier per sq ft; area filters and price per sq ft are wrong

findings.documented: timestamps are ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z suffix, everywhere in the API
findings.actual: listings posted_at has no Z or offset and is IST wall-clock time, not UTC. The feed ends at 2026-09-09T23:54, just before the IST reference moment; read as UTC, these would be after the reference. Rentals do send UTC with Z
findings.how_found: compared the latest posted_at per portal with the reference moment, and with rentals whose UTC times stop at 17:03Z
findings.impact: parsing as UTC shifts every listing by 5.5 hours and moves records across day and week boundaries (128 vs 115 in the last 7 days)

findings.documented: sort_by=posted_at sorts listings by posting time
findings.actual: sort_by=posted_at only orders by calendar day; within a day records are unordered (2026-01-13T20:12, 20:10, 20:23, 03:22 ...), in both directions
findings.how_found: checked whether each page returned with sort_by=posted_at was monotonic in the full timestamp
findings.impact: "newest first" is wrong within every day

findings.documented: total_listings on a project always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns
findings.actual: project_id is not a filter: /v1/listings?project_id=P30381 returns all 3800 records
findings.how_found: compared the filtered response with the unfiltered one
findings.impact: a project page cannot fetch its listings from the server

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees
findings.actual: price_min and price_max are floats in lakhs or crores with no unit field: values below 10 are crores (1.01-4.47), values from 32.6 to 99.9 are lakhs. For example P30001 has price_min 80.0 (Rs 80 lakh) and price_max 3.22 (Rs 3.22 crore). sort_by=price_max orders by the converted rupee value
findings.how_found: price_min was usually numerically larger than price_max; the values split into two ranges with nothing between 4.47 and 32.6
findings.impact: project prices are unusable as documented; min > max for most projects

findings.documented: total_listings is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with the listings endpoint
findings.actual: for 95 of 440 projects total_listings does not match the number of live listings in /v1/listings with that project_id (it matches exactly for the other 345); 41 of the wrong ones report 0
findings.how_found: counted live listings per project_id from the full crawl and compared
findings.impact: project pages show wrong availability

findings.documented: deposit is the security deposit in rupees
findings.actual: for all 307 zerobroker rentals deposit is a number of months of rent (2-10), not rupees; other portals send rupees (2-10 times the rent)
findings.how_found: looked at deposit / price for every rental; one portal had values under 100
findings.impact: a Rs 30,000/month flat shows a Rs 4 deposit
